# Case development: a minimum operating baseline

This is a **proposed application baseline** for Manifold (the Execution and Operating Model standard). It describes how a human, agents and supporting programs can turn an idea or existing situation into an attributable needs–requirements–systems model, maintain it, and expose gaps. The human authorized developing this baseline; its particular process, records and responsibilities remain proposals to examine through use.

The immediate problem is concrete: the initial self-application map names broad purposes but does not sufficiently explain how to onboard affected participants, turn their accounts into justified requirements, construct system descriptions, or keep the resulting model coherent. The [detailed self-application](../../../source-locators.md#source-e24d99d3d712b164) supplies contextual needs, derived requirements and candidate arrangements. The [discussion record](../../../source-locators.md#source-f1e51950d9798820) preserves the direction and remaining uncertainty.

## Boundary and responsibility

Inside this baseline: discovery and clarification, representation of requirements and candidate arrangements, provenance, internal consistency, justified predicted contribution, visible gaps, scoped decisions and maintenance of the model. Manifold can also represent and interpret externally supplied assessments using its accepted [fulfillment contract](../assessment/requirement-and-need-fulfillment.md).

Outside this baseline: implementing the described external system and conducting its detailed operational verification. An arrangement is not proven useful merely because its description is internally consistent. A program that checks reference integrity cannot establish the adequacy of a need or a contribution argument.

The case model and the shared standard have different responsibility boundaries. A case steward coordinates its content and unresolved work; participants remain the sources of their accounts, and a case decision needs an appropriate authority. The standard maintainer owns changes to shared rules within their remit. Shared storage or the same human holding several roles does not merge these authorities.

## Proposed cooperating arrangements

The original S2 application arrangement is expanded into four candidate subsystems. S1 continues to maintain the shared standard. These are arrangements of people, assignments, information and supporting mechanisms; neither a process title nor a folder is sufficient to establish a system. The [worked descriptions](../../../source-locators.md#source-3218084749aedf19) identify their elements, structure, behavior, inputs, outputs and limits.

| Arrangement | Distinct purpose | Principal output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| S2.1 — Discover participants and needs | Preserve whose situation and desired outcome are being described. | Participation map, source accounts, candidate needs, unanswered questions. |
| S2.2 — Form and reconcile requirements | Explain candidate commitments, their origins and conflicting conditions. | Requirement set, criteria, contribution rationale, conflicts and dispositions. |
| S2.3 — Model candidate arrangements | Explain interacting parts, resources, responsibilities and behavior. | Alternative system descriptions and proposed allocations. |
| S2.4 — Review alignment and coverage | Expose unsupported, absent or conflicting connections. | Coverage view, findings, returned questions and a bounded decision basis. |
| S1 — Maintain the shared standard | Resolve reusable meaning and rule issues revealed by cases. | Applicable standard revisions, decisions and adoption guidance. |

They share a case record rather than repeatedly copying information into isolated documents. Information can enter at discovery, an existing requirement, a vision, a system proposal or an external result. The producer/recipient relationships are explicit; there is no mandatory waterfall.

## Structural information kept in the case

These are logical records, not a demand for one file, database table or new frontmatter kind per row. Linked information is preferable to copying it. Use established document identity and provenance conventions for documents; a final machine schema remains a separate open design choice.

| Logical record | Minimum recoverable information for this baseline | Responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Case brief | Subject, practical question, purpose, boundary, relevant environment, applicable standard revision and intended use of the model. | Case sponsor supplies direction; steward maintains the record. |
| Participants and assignments | Affected groups and source representatives; dotted role labels, actual assignees or vacancies, scope and authority basis; missing representation. | Stakeholders confirm their own accounts; steward tracks gaps and bindings. |
| Source account and interpretation | Original statement or source locator, who supplied it and when, context, agent/human interpretation, unresolved meaning and any participant correction. | Discovery contributor records; source participant can correct their account. |
| Need | Participant(s), situation, desired condition, motivating problem or purpose, source basis and whether the interpretation is confirmed, disputed or unconfirmed. | Requirements author drafts; relevant participant feedback is retained. |
| Requirement | Subject, statement, applicability, origin and justification, criterion or unresolved criterion, standing, and relevant need links where known. | Requirements author drafts; commitment needs identified case authority. |
| Arrangement and interface | Purpose and boundary, constituent elements, dependencies, resources, process/state descriptions, interfaces, responsibility bindings and alternatives. | Designer maintains; affected operators or maintainers supply constraints where available. |
| Contribution | Referenced need/requirement/arrangement sets and revisions, relation meaning, rationale, conditions, and joint versus alternative contribution. | Designer proposes; reviewer challenges; steward tracks unresolved claims. |
| Issue, trade-off and decision | Exact affected statements, reason, options and consequences, decision authority or vacancy, disposition, residual shortfall and follow-up owner. | Reviewer raises; assigned recipient resolves or escalates; authority decides where needed. |
| Assessment received from outside | Assessed subject/revision, criterion, required and examined conditions, evidence source, reasoning, conclusion and limits under the accepted assessment contract. | Reviewer checks interpretability; original assessor/source remains attributable. |
| Revision and case baseline | What changed, why, affected links, preserved earlier basis, open issues and the decision to use a specific revision for a specified purpose. | Case steward coordinates; sponsor/other appropriate authority decides scoped use. |

A need being *reported by* a representative is different from that representative being its *beneficiary*. A requirement being *derived from* a source is different from being *accepted by* an authority. A system being *part of* another is different from *depending on* it or *contributing to* a requirement. Use the [relationship vocabulary](../ontology/relationships.md) to keep those distinctions visible.

## Discovery and interview loop

Start by explaining the case's purpose and asking who uses, operates, maintains, funds, constrains or is affected by the proposed arrangement. These are prompts for finding relevant perspectives, not six compulsory distinct people. Programs are represented through declared consuming functions and interface evidence; an agent must not fabricate a program's testimony or simulate absent humans as evidence.

For each relevant perspective:

1. Capture the situation, original request, desired change and why it matters. Retain a request for a particular tool as a requested solution while exploring its underlying purpose.
2. Ask what conditions matter, what presently goes wrong, what must remain true, and what outcomes or compromises would be unacceptable.
3. Ask what would make success recognizable, which other people or systems depend on it, and whose account may disagree.
4. Replay the interpretation and its proposed need/requirement links. Record confirmation, correction, disagreement or lack of response against the exact interpretation; silence is not agreement.
5. Repeat where the answer exposes a material gap. Hand off confirmed and unconfirmed statements with their status visible; leave each unresolved question with a recipient and next action or explicit vacancy.

The loop can stop for a stated purpose when the relevant accounts are represented well enough for the next activity, and remaining gaps are explicitly dispositioned. There is no fixed interview count and no claim of universal completeness. A reversible design exploration may proceed with assumptions; an unresolved condition must not be hidden to claim readiness for a commitment that depends on it.

## Handoffs and return paths

| Producer → recipient | What makes the input usable | If it is incomplete or challenged |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Discovery → requirements | Source-bearing interpretations, participant context and unresolved questions at an identifiable revision. | Requirements contributor returns specific clarification questions; disputed statements remain separate. |
| Vision/interface source → requirements | The source, relevant constraint or purpose, and its claimed authority/applicability. | Preserve the candidate input; flag unsupported applicability rather than inventing a need or authority. |
| Requirements → arrangement design | Statements, conditions, criteria or open criterion questions, and proposed/accepted standing. | Designer returns missing constraints or contradictions; exploratory options may state provisional assumptions. |
| Arrangement design → coverage review | Parts, behavior, resources, alternatives and allocations with contribution rationale. | Reviewer identifies the exact unsupported connection and routes it to design, requirements or discovery. |
| External assessor → coverage review | Assessment subject/revision, criterion, evidence and examined conditions. | Keep the source account; the affected judgment remains unknown where missing context prevents interpretation. |
| Coverage review → case steward/decision authority | Findings, affected scope, residual gaps and proposed next actions. | No silent acceptance; the steward identifies a decision recipient, requests clarification or records an unassigned decision. |
| Case → shared standard maintenance | A specific rule ambiguity or gap, the case consequence and relevant rule revision. | Standard maintainer distinguishes a local exception from a shared rule change; the case retains its own disposition. |
| Revised standard → case steward | Changed rule, rationale, compatibility consequences and applicable revision. | Case steward checks impact; adoption, deferral or incompatibility remains explicit rather than silently rewriting the case. |

A returned question is work with an owner or an explicit missing owner. “Review failed” without a referenced statement, reason and recipient is not a useful handoff.

## How humans, agents and programs uphold the baseline

| Participant | Work it can contribute | Limit of the result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Human | Supply lived context, correct interpretations, set priorities, authorize scoped commitments and decide trade-offs within a real remit. | One human does not automatically represent every group or possess every decision right. |
| Agent | Conduct authorized interviews, draft transformations, propose structures, inspect meaning, challenge claims and prepare updates. | A plausible inference remains attributable as an inference; a review does not create acceptance authority. |
| Program | Check a declared subset of explicit record/reference rules, detect selected missing values or stale references, and project a selected model revision. | Supported checks must be enumerated. Passing them does not establish semantic adequacy, full coverage or operational fulfillment. |

Program functions remain prospective in this baseline. Manual or agent-supported performance is possible while their contracts are developed. Each execution needs actual assignments; a role label alone does not identify who performed the work.

Use three separate review questions before calling a revision ready for its intended use:

- **Record integrity:** Can the supported checks resolve the intended identities, revisions and required information, or explicitly report what they cannot check?
- **Meaning and contribution:** Can a reviewer explain the transformations and contributions, including missing participants, assumptions, trade-offs and unsupported claims?
- **Scoped disposition:** Is the authority and intended use known, with consequential open issues accepted for that use, returned for resolution or explicitly preventing the dependent commitment?

These questions describe a proposed operating practice. They do not introduce a universal approval workflow or turn every unanswered question into a block on all development. Distinguish record standing, progress of an activity, case readiness for a purpose, and fulfillment of a requirement.

## Maintenance and change

A changed source, interpretation, requirement, arrangement or external result can reopen any affected stage. Preserve the earlier revision and mark the affected links and conclusions for reconsideration. A later successful result does not erase an earlier failure; a new requirement does not retroactively govern an old assessment without an explicit new analysis.

The case steward coordinates this work across S2.1–S2.4. S1 is involved when the shared standard itself needs a change. Cases may use different standard revisions; compatibility and adoption need to remain understandable. Keep the summary map and program views tied to the same selected case revision or identify their differences.

## What makes this a useful first baseline

A first case should let a reader move from a source statement through its interpretation and proposed requirement to a candidate arrangement, inspect its actual structural elements and handoffs, and see both a supported connection and a remaining gap. It should also survive a changed requirement without losing the basis of earlier judgments.

The [self-application refinement](../../../source-locators.md#source-e24d99d3d712b164) makes these obligations concrete. The next useful work is to exercise one complete interview-to-model loop and its return path on Manifold itself, then examine the multi-participant, shared-subsystem and revision probes recorded there. More named needs or boxes alone do not demonstrate adequacy for larger problems.
